{"document": {"acknowledgments": [{"summary": "These vulnerabilities were found during internal security testing."}], "category": "csaf_security_advisory", "csaf_version": "2.0", "notes": [{"category": "summary", "text": "Multiple vulnerabilities in the Operation, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) feature of Cisco NX-OS Software, known as Next Generation OAM (NGOAM), could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges or cause a denial of service (DoS) condition on an affected device.

These vulnerabilities are due to improper input validation of IP traffic when NGOAM is enabled. An attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by sending crafted packets to an IP interface on an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges and could cause process crashes, which could result in a reload of the device and a DoS condition.

Note: Feature requirements vary for each vulnerability. For details, see the Vulnerable Products ["#vp"] section of this advisory.

Cisco has released software updates that address these vulnerabilities. There are no workarounds that address these vulnerabilities.



This advisory is part of a group of advisories. For a complete list of the advisories and links to them, see Cisco Advance Notification for Publication of October 7, 2026, Security Advisories ["https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-notice-fBn58ELx"]. For further documentation of improvements and fixes in Cisco NX-OS Software, see Cisco NX-OS Software Security Hardening Release: October 2026 ["https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-hardening-nxosw1-cWzSbtR"].", "title": "Summary"}, {"category": "general", "text": "These vulnerabilities affect Cisco Nexus 3000 Series Switches and Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches in standalone NX-OS mode if NGOAM is enabled and specific features are configured, as detailed in the following list:

CVE-2026-76485: To be affected by this vulnerability, the switch must have NGOAM enabled. That is the only requirement.
CVE-2026-76486: To be affected by this vulnerability, the switch must have NGOAM enabled and either Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) or Network Virtualization (NV) Overlay enabled. NV Overlay also requires a VXLAN Ethernet VPN (EVPN) VXLAN Network Identifier (VNI) mapped to a Network Virtualization Endpoint (NVE) interface with at least one peer VXLAN Tunnel Endpoint (VTEP) learned (for example, BGP EVPN or an ingress-replication static peer).
CVE-2026-76501: To be affected by this vulnerability, the switch must have both NGOAM and SRv6 enabled.

Note: Cisco Nexus 3000 Series switches do not support SRv6, and only a subset of Cisco Nexus 9000 Series switches support SRv6. For more information, see Cisco Nexus 9000 Series NX-OS SRv6 Configuration Guide, Release 10.6(x) ["https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/dcn/nx-os/nexus9000/106x/configuration/srv6/cisco-nexus-9000-series-nx-os-srv6-configuration-guide-106x/m-configuring-srv6-oam.html"].

Determine the Status of NGOAM

To determine whether a device is configured with NGOAM enabled, use the show feature | include ngoam command at the Cisco NX-OS CLI. The following example shows NGOAM enabled on a device that is running Cisco NX-OS Software:


switch# show feature | include ngoam
ngoam                  1          enabled

Determine the Status of NV Overlay

To determine whether a device is configured with NV Overlay enabled, use the show feature | include nve command at the Cisco NX-OS CLI. The following example shows NV Overlay enabled on a device that is running Cisco NX-OS Software:


switch# show feature | include nve
nve                    1          disabled
switch# configure
switch(config)# feature nv overlay
switch(config)# show feature | include nve
nve                    1          enabled

Determine the Status of the NV Overlay VXLAN EVPN VNI

To determine whether a device is configured with VXLAN EVPN VNI mapped on an NVE interface with at least one peer VTEP learned, use the following commands at the Cisco NX-OS CLI:

show running-config | begin "interface nve"
show nve vni
show nve peers

If all three commands return data, as shown in the following example, then the device may be affected by CVE-2026-76486.


switch# show running-config | begin "interface nve"
interface nve1
  source-interface loopback1
  member vni 160010 mcast-group 203.0.113.1
  member vni 160020 mcast-group 203.0.113.1
  no shutdown

switch# show nve vni
Interface  VNI      Multicast-group  VNI State
---------  -------- ---------------  ---------
nve1       160010   203.0.113.1      Up

switch# show nve peers
Interface  Peer-IP      Peer-State
---------  ------------ ----------
nve1       192.168.2.1  Up

Determine the Status of SRv6

To determine whether a device is configured with SRv6 enabled, use the show feature | include srv6 command at the Cisco NX-OS CLI. The following example shows SRv6 enabled on a device that is running Cisco NX-OS Software:


switch# show feature | include srv6
srv6                   1          enabled", "title": "Vulnerable Products"}, {"category": "general", "text": "Only products listed in the Vulnerable Products ["#vp"] section of this advisory are known to be affected by this vulnerability.

Cisco has confirmed that this vulnerability does not affect the following Cisco products:

Firepower 1000 Series
Firepower 2100 Series
Firepower 4100 Series
Firepower 9300 Security Appliances
MDS 9000 Series Multilayer Switches
Nexus 7000 Series Switches
Nexus 9000 Series Fabric Switches in ACI mode
Secure Firewall 200 Series
Secure Firewall 1200 Series
Secure Firewall 3100 Series
Secure Firewall 4200 Series
Secure Firewall 6100 Series
UCS 6300 Series Fabric Interconnects
UCS 6400 Series Fabric Interconnects
UCS 6500 Series Fabric Interconnects
UCS 6600 Series Fabric Interconnects
UCS X-Series Direct Fabric Interconnect 9108 100G", "title": "Products Confirmed Not Vulnerable"}, {"category": "general", "text": "The VXLAN NGOAM feature on Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches provides loop detection and mitigation capabilities, particularly for Layer 3 interfaces and VXLAN OAM functionalities. For more information, see Cisco Nexus 9000 Series NX-OS VXLAN Configuration Guide, Release 10.4(x) ["https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/dcn/nx-os/nexus9000/104x/configuration/vxlan/cisco-nexus-9000-series-nx-os-vxlan-configuration-guide-release-104x/m-configuring-vxlan-oam.html"].

The SRv6 NGOAM feature on Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches provides monitoring and diagnostic capabilities for SRv6 paths. It assists with fault detection and troubleshooting by using IPv6 ping and pathtrace mechanisms to verify path connectivity and isolate forwarding problems in the network. For more information, see Cisco Nexus 9000 Series NX-OS SRv6 Configuration Guide, Release 10.6(x) ["https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/dcn/nx-os/nexus9000/106x/configuration/srv6/cisco-nexus-9000-series-nx-os-srv6-configuration-guide-106x/m-configuring-srv6-oam.html"].", "title": "Details"}, {"category": "general", "text": "There are no workarounds that address these vulnerabilities.

If the NGOAM feature is not required, disabling it removes the attack vector and is a mitigation for all three vulnerabilities. Disable the NGOAM by using the Cisco NX-OS CLI command no feature ngoam in global configuration mode on a Cisco Nexus 3000 Series or 9000 Series Switch.

While this mitigation has been deployed and was proven successful in a test environment, customers should determine the applicability and effectiveness in their own environment and under their own use conditions. Customers should be aware that any workaround or mitigation that is implemented may negatively impact the functionality or performance of their network based on intrinsic customer deployment scenarios and limitations. Customers should not deploy any workarounds or mitigations before first evaluating the applicability to their own environment and any impact to such environment.



Live Protect Shields

Cisco has released Live Protect shields ["https://software.cisco.com/download/products?swtypemdfid=286346710&relver=10.6(3)"] for CVE-2026-76485, CVE-2026-76486, and CVE-2026-76501 to temporarily mitigate these vulnerabilities for Cisco NX-OS Software.

For information about Live Protect for Cisco NX-OS Software, see Cisco Nexus 9000 Series NX-OS Security Configuration Guide ["https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/dcn/nx-os/nexus9000/106x/configuration/security/cisco-nexus-9000-series-nx-os-security-configuration-guide-release-106x/m-secure-nx-os-with-live-protect.html"].

Note: Live Protect shields are temporary mitigations to bridge the gap until software updates can be scheduled.
